note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 3: 'MUST NOT drop (as part of GTSM processing) packets classified as Trusted or Unknown.' Re-read the four changed units. TestGTSMDeliversAnICMPErrorNoSessionClaims: Unknown ICMPv4 errors at TTL 1 (other port, other host, quoted header with options spelling port 179) must raise InType3 by one and match no term. TestGTSMListenerUnknownNotDropped: SYNs at TTL/hop limit 1 from a non-GTSM peer, an unconfigured address, the GTSM peer to another port, and an IPv6 non-GTSM host must each get a SYN-ACK with no term matched. TestGTSMListenerSYNAtFloorAccepted and its IPv6 twin: a SYN at the 255 floor gets a SYN-ACK, the injected ACK yields an accepted connection from the peer, and no term counter moved. Socket-floor units in rfc5082_ttl_gtsm_linux_test.go are unchanged. Residuals as before: only floor 255 is driven at the listener; listenerAtFloorProof does not itself read that the listen rule is installed.
